svg.title: Luading Disting NT pixel UI components — 131 components, 665 variants

g.text: Luading · Disting NT pixel UI components
131 components · 665 declared state variants · artwork shown at 1× logical pixel scale · import this SVG directly into Figma

g.title: Panel frame — A compact section boundary with optional focus emphasis.
Section header — A tiny dynamic label with an active underline.
Status lamp — A shape-coded gate, pulse, warning, or error indicator driven by script state.
Divider ruler — A five-tick section divider with a script-positioned active reference.
Label value row — A compact dynamic label and value readout with focus, stale, and error treatments.
State badge — A short text badge with inactive, inverted-active, warning, and error treatments.
Tabs segmented selector — A three-mode selector whose chosen tab is marked by both fill and an underline.
Page indicator — A compact four-page strip with a position marker and explicit wrap, disabled, and error treatments.
Focus selection brackets — An orthogonal corner overlay for focus or selection with warning, error, and inactive treatments.
Empty unavailable marker — An explicit text fallback for empty, waiting, unavailable, and error states.
Input jack — An inward-marked logical input with activity and level.
Output jack — An outward-marked logical output with activity and clipping.
Bidirectional jack — A configurable utility jack whose direction is explicit in every state.
Stereo paired jacks — Compact left/right jacks with linked, split, and disabled structures.
Normalled pair — Two logical ports with an explicit default route and broken-normal state.
Labelled port tile — A standard channel tile combining direction, jack, short label, signal kind, and level.
Split multiple node — A one-to-three routing node with explicit active, partial, and disabled branch treatments.
Merge mix node — A three-to-one routing node with independent input activity and a clipped output apex.
Routing matrix cell — A compact crosspoint with off, connected, modulated, selected, and conflict shapes.
Patch link flow line — A directional route with idle, animated flow, selection, blocked, and feedback treatments.
Bus rail and tap — A shared bus diagram with three script-selected taps and explicit activity, overrange, and disabled states.
Router switch — A one-to-three route whose selected destination and exceptional switching states are geometrically explicit.
Send return loop — A compact directional effects loop with explicit open, closed, feedback, bypass, and overload geometry.
Momentary button — A compact labelled trigger, reset, tap, or latch button.
Toggle switch — A two-position switch for mute, invert, freeze, or enable.
Horizontal fader — A compact linear control with base and effective value markers.
Three-way switch — A left, centre, or right selector for polarity, range, or direction.
Bipolar fader — A centre-zero fader for offset, pan, attenuversion, swing, or signed CV.
Range slider — Three-marker minimum, maximum, and current range control with invalid and clamped states.
Vertical fader — A compact channel fader with separate base and effective-value handles.
Rotary knob — A compact continuous control with base, effective, focus, limit, and disabled marks.
Encoder ring — A stepped encoder indicator with turning direction, push, focus, and disabled marks.
XY pad vector point — A compact two-axis control with a script-positioned point, optional centre vector, focus, and clipping marks.
Soft takeover control — A pickup display that keeps the target and physical control positions visibly separate until they meet.
Numeric unit readout — A script-formatted value and unit readout with distinct changing, invalid, and overflow treatments.
Choice readout — A script-formatted mode or destination readout with committed, focused, pending, invalid, and disabled treatments.
Seven segment small — Small seven-segment digit. Set State to a string "0"–"9", "-", "blank", or "custom"; custom exposes segments A–G. Combine independently wired digits for longer numbers.
Seven segment medium — Medium seven-segment digit. Set State to a string "0"–"9", "-", "blank", or "custom"; custom exposes segments A–G. Combine independently wired digits for longer numbers.
Seven segment large — Large seven-segment digit. Set State to a string "0"–"9", "-", "blank", or "custom"; custom exposes segments A–G. Combine independently wired digits for longer numbers.
Signal type badge — An original compact glyph for common modular signal roles.
Waveform glyph — A waveform silhouette with an optional script-driven phase cursor.
Direction badge — A compact arrow badge for input, output, thru, send, return, or feedback.
Polarity range badge — A compact shape-coded qualifier for positive, negative, bipolar, inverted, centred, or clamped CV.
Unit badge — A compact unit label for voltage, pitch, time, rate, level, ratio, or steps.
Channel voice badge — A consistent channel identity badge with active, mute, solo, and selection shapes.
Attenuator — A level processor tile with a normalized amount display.
Mixer — A two-input sum tile with independent input level bars.
Clamp processor — A transfer-shape tile with explicit lower and upper bounds.
Sample and hold — A sampling tile that separates acquisition, hold, bypass, and error states.
Logic processor — A gate-logic tile with independent input and output truth marks.
Bernoulli router — A probability-controlled A/B event router with an explicit most-recent decision.
Attenuverter processor — A centre-zero level and polarity tile with explicit processing, bypass, saturation, and error states.
Gain VCA processor — A compact gain and VCA tile with explicit control activity, bypass, saturation, and error states.
Slew processor — A time-response tile that distinguishes rising, falling, holding, bypass, and error states.
Pitch quantizer processor — A pitch-grid tile that separates input, accepted output, rejected, bypass, and error states.
Comparator processor — A two-input comparison tile with explicit low/high result, selection, bypass, and error geometry.
Clock transform processor — A clock utility tile for divide, multiply, swing, ratchet, and burst operations with script-owned phase, pulse, and lock state.
Feedback utility — A directional send/return processor with script-owned feedback amount, freeze, instability, clipping, and bypass states.
Polarity utility processor — Offset and inversion operations that complete the level-and-polarity processor family.
Crossfade multiply processor — Sum, average, crossfade, and ring/multiply signal-combination operations.
Waveshaper processor — Limiter, window, rectification, and fold transfer-shape operations.
Timing utility processor — Low-pass, delay, gate-delay, gate-length, and pulse-width time-response operations.
Sampling utility processor — Track-and-hold, latch, and bounded shift-register sampling operations.

g.data-name: Sampling utility processor / Track and hold
g.title: Sampling utility processor / Track and hold
Quantization utility processor — Grid, step, and scale-mask quantization operations beyond the pitch-quantizer tile.
Comparison utility processor — Window comparator, zero-crossing, minimum, and maximum comparison operations.
Probability utility processor — Probability-gate, skip, and random-select operations with explicit script-owned decisions.
Switching utility processor — Mux, selector, sequential-switch, and sample-router operations.
Unipolar bar meter — A zero-to-one fill meter with an independent peak marker.
Bipolar bar meter — A centre-zero meter for signed CV, pan, offset, or modulation.
Segmented meter — An eight-part coarse meter for stages, density, progress, or load categories.
Vertical channel meter — A narrow channel meter with script-owned level and peak hold.
Threshold window meter — An input marker and two threshold rails for comparator or safe-range displays.
Modulation range meter — A base and effective value display bounded by authored modulation limits.
Gate trigger activity — A shape-coded gate level and edge-flash indicator driven entirely by script state.
Envelope contour — An ADSR contour with script-owned stage geometry and a distinct current phase and level marker.
Phase clock ring — A compact phase and division ring with stopped, running, searching, locked, and error shapes.
Note range ladder — A compact pitch ladder showing input, output, accepted range, quantization, rejection, and invalid bounds.
XY vector meter — A non-interactive two-axis signal meter with a script-supplied point, radius limit, stale, clip, and error treatments.
Bounded scope strip — An eight-sample scope whose chronological normalized history is supplied explicitly by script state.
Step cell — A compact gate step with distinct off, on, accent, tie, and mute states.
Value step cell — A vertical value step for pitch or CV sequences.
Playhead cursor — A script-positioned cursor overlay for a sequencer row or compact grid.
Loop range bracket — Explicit loop endpoints with pending and reversed-range treatments.
Transport strip — A compact stopped, playing, paused, recording, armed, or waiting-clock status strip.
Pattern page strip — Pattern or page navigation with separate queued, playing, dirty, and error marks.
Tracker row — A micro tracker event row with note, gate, effect, current, selection, mute, and empty treatments.
Mini keyboard note row — A one-octave note row with separate note, root, output, rejection, and disabled marks.

g.data-name: Mini keyboard note row / Input note
g.title: Mini keyboard note row / Input note

g.data-name: Mini keyboard note row / Output note
g.title: Mini keyboard note row / Output note
Eight-step pitch CV lane — An eight-step pitch or CV lane with independent values, playhead, mute, clip, and error treatments.
Eight-step gate row — A bounded eight-step gate pattern with independent steps, algorithm-owned playhead, output activity, mute, record, and error states.
Probability accent lane — An eight-step authored probability lane with a separate most-recent fired, skipped, or accented event marker.
Eight-step Euclidean ring — A bounded eight-position Euclidean rhythm ring with explicit hits, current position, rotation, mute, and invalid states.
Four-stage strip — A bounded ramp, hold, step, and release strip with script-owned levels, current stage, gate, loop, finish, and invalid states.
Sixteen-step row — A bounded sixteen-step pattern row with independent gates, playhead, loop endpoints, run, record, mute, and error states.
Eight-step drum lane — A bounded drum lane with independent hits and accents, playhead, header flash, mute, solo, and error states.
Radial groove ring — A bounded two-lane, sixteen-position rhythm ring with explicit authored hits, playhead, swing, mute, and error states; it has a deliberately higher draw cost.
Drum voice glyph — An original classic-analog kick glyph with hit, accent, and mute states.
Drum voice tile — A labelled drum channel with voice event and level meter.
Drum step cell — A rhythm step with distinct hit, accent, flam, roll, probability, ghost, and mute marks.
Fill roll indicator — A bounded fill or roll meter that separates armed, firing, and finished states.
Two voice drum overview — A two-voice performance view with independent hit, accent, mute, level, and step inputs.

g.title: Two voice drum overview / Clock lost
Punchy hybrid snare glyph — An original angular snare glyph with hit, accent, mute, selection, and solo overlays.
Classic analog snare glyph — An original rounded shell-and-noise snare glyph for the Classic analog drum family.
Punchy hybrid kick glyph — An original angular shell-and-transient kick glyph for the Punchy hybrid drum family.
Classic analog clap glyph — An original layered transient glyph for the Classic analog drum family.
Punchy hybrid clap glyph — An original angular layered-clap glyph for the Punchy hybrid drum family.
Classic analog rim claves glyph — An original paired-stick and rim transient glyph for the Classic analog drum family.

g.title: Clock source badge — A clock source and lock-state badge with a phase marker.
MIDI activity — A script-level MIDI receive, send, filter, or error indicator.
I2C activity — A script-owned I2C transaction indicator that performs no bus work from drawing.
Preset state marker — Script-owned preset feedback for clean, changed, saving, saved, or error state.
Warning error banner — A compact text-required warning or error treatment with latched and dismissed states.
Busy progress indicator — A bounded script-owned progress display with idle, working, complete, and error states.
